Write \(E_0=E_{P_{0,O}}\). The strict inequalities in the statement are theorem-point conditions, not changes to either model class. Their role is to ensure that every sufficiently small two-sided path used below remains within the weak support, moment, SC-rank, and spectral margins. Local constancy of \(\operatorname{rank}(\Omega_x)\) permits one independent coordinate system throughout that neighborhood.

By \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\),
\[
 q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=\delta_1^0(x)\mathbf 1_J-D(x),
 \qquad A_{\mathrm{PT}}=I_J-J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}.
 \tag{1}
\]
Because \(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}\mathbf 1_J=J\),
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}\mathbf 1_J=0,
 \qquad A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot q_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\dot D(x).
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus profiling the unrestricted scalar path \(\dot\delta_1^0(x)\) leaves precisely the observed derivative of \(-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\). The matrix \(A_{\mathrm{PT}}\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\{v:\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}v=0\}\), so it has rank \(J-1\). If \(\widetilde R_{D,x}\) represents \(\dot D(x)\), then \(R_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}\widetilde R_{D,x}\), whence
\[
 \operatorname{rank}E_0[R_{\mathrm{PT},x}R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}]
 \le J-1.
 \tag{3}
\]
Positive definiteness of the covariance form on \(\operatorname{range}(A_{\mathrm{PT}})\) makes the inequality an equality.

For SC put \(\Pi_x=B(x)\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}\). The strict SC-rank condition makes \(\Pi_x\) the orthogonal projector onto the \(J\)-dimensional column space of \(B(x)\). At an SC law, \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\). Differentiating \(\Pi_xB(x)=B(x)\) and then \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=(I_T-\Pi_x)a(x)\) gives
\[
 \dot r_{\mathrm{SC},x}
 =(I_T-\Pi_x)\{\dot a(x)-\dot B(x)w(x)\}.
 \tag{4}
\]
The covariance range of \(R_{\mathrm{SC},x}\) is therefore contained in \(\operatorname{range}(I_T-\Pi_x)\), whose dimension is \(T-J\). This proves the SC rank ceiling; positive definiteness of the residualized covariance form on that range gives equality.

For every occupied cell, quotient differentiation gives
\[
 \dot\mu_{g,t}(x;s)
 =E_0\!\left[
 \frac{\mathbf 1\{G=g,X=x\}}{p_X(x)p_g(x)}
 \{Y_t-\mu_{g,t}(x)\}s\right].
 \tag{5}
\]
The denominator is positive by strict cell mass and overlap. The bracketed function has conditional mean zero given \((G,X)\). Both \(r_{b,x}\) and \(C_b(x)\) are differentiable finite-dimensional functions of the cell means at the stated full-rank point. Applying the ordinary chain rule to (5) constructs the versions of \(R_{b,x}\) and \(g^{\circ}_{b,x}\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\), including their conditional-residual normalizations.

We next characterize the tangents. The PT observed projection is locally the zero set of \(r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=-A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)\), because
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}D(x)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 D(x)=c(x)\mathbf 1_J
 \tag{6}
\]
for a scalar \(c(x)\); the missing treated untreated final mean may then be assigned as \(\mu_{1,T-1}(x)+c(x)\). The SC observed projection is locally the zero set of \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=(I_T-\Pi_x)a(x)\), since full column rank gives
\[
 r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a(x)=B(x)w(x),
 \tag{7}
\]
and the missing treated untreated final mean may be assigned as \(w(x)^{\prime}\mu_{C,T}(x)\). No anticipation makes every preperiod and donor mean in these constructions observed. Small deterministic shifts of the missing treated untreated final outcome implement the required full-data means; the observed law is unchanged by that lift.

Differentiating the branch equations along a branch-preserving path yields
\[
 E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0\qquad\text{for every }x.
 \tag{8}
\]
For the converse, retain a maximal linearly independent coordinate vector \(R_b^*\). By local constant rank the same coordinates remain independent nearby. Its Gram matrix is positive definite. Truncating and recentering its coordinates yields a bounded vector \(v\) such that \(M=E_0[R_b^*v^{\prime}]\) is nonsingular. For a bounded mean-zero score \(s\) satisfying (8), consider the two-sided exponential tilt
\[
 \frac{dP_{O,\varepsilon,c}}{dP_{0,O}}
 =\frac{\exp\{\varepsilon s+c^{\prime}v\}}
 {E_0[\exp\{\varepsilon s+c^{\prime}v\}]},
 \qquad
 F(\varepsilon,c)=r_b^*(P_{O,\varepsilon,c}).
 \tag{9}
\]
Boundedness of \(s\) and \(v\) makes (9) well defined for both signs of sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\) and \(c\). The finite support, the strict probability and fourth-moment slack, and the strict rank and spectral gaps imply by continuity that these tilted laws remain inside all weak model margins. Differentiation under the integral is justified by the bounded likelihood ratio and the fourth-moment envelope. At the origin,
\[
 F(0,0)=0,
 \qquad \partial_cF(0,0)=M,
 \qquad \partial_{\varepsilon}F(0,0)=E_0[R_b^*s]=0.
 \tag{10}
\]
Differentiability gives
\[
 F(\varepsilon,c)=F(\varepsilon,0)+Mc+\zeta(\varepsilon,c),
 \qquad F(\varepsilon,0)=o(\varepsilon),
 \tag{11}
\]
where, on a sufficiently small ball, the Lipschitz constant of \(c\mapsto M^{-1}\zeta(\varepsilon,c)\) is at most \(1/2\). Hence
\[
 \mathcal K_\varepsilon(c)
 =-M^{-1}\{F(\varepsilon,0)+\zeta(\varepsilon,c)\}
 \tag{12}
\]
maps a ball of radius \(C|\varepsilon|\) into itself for a fixed sufficiently large \(C\) and is a contraction there. Its iterates from zero are Cauchy, since successive differences shrink by a factor at most \(1/2\). Their limit \(c(\varepsilon)\) satisfies \(F(\varepsilon,c(\varepsilon))=0\), and (11) gives \(c(\varepsilon)=o(\varepsilon)\). Therefore the corrected two-sided path has score \(s\). The full-data assignments following (6)--(7) lift it into branch \(b\).

For a general \(s\in L_0^2(P_{0,O})\) satisfying (8), truncate and recenter it to \(\widetilde s_k\), and set
\[
 s_k=\widetilde s_k-v^{\prime}M^{-1}E_0[R_b^*\widetilde s_k].
 \tag{13}
\]
Then \(s_k\) is bounded, \(E_0[R_b^*s_k]=0\), and \(s_k\to s\) in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\): the correction tends to zero because \(\widetilde s_k\to s\) in \(L^2\) and \(E_0[R_b^*s]=0\). Taking the closure in \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\text{-}tangents}\) proves
\[
 \mathcal T_b(P_0)=\{s\in\mathcal H_{P_0}:E_0[R_{b,x}s]=0\text{ for all }x\}.
 \tag{14}
\]

It remains to differentiate the stratum composition. Put \(q_x=P_O(G=1,X=x)\). Strict cell mass and overlap imply \(\pi_1=\sum_xq_x>0\). Since \(\nu_x=q_x/\pi_1\), quotient differentiation yields
\[
 \dot\nu_x(s)
 =E_0\!\left[\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=1\}}{\pi_1}
 \{\mathbf 1\{X=x\}-\nu_x\}s\right].
 \tag{15}
\]
Using \(\theta_b=\sum_x\nu_xC_b(x)\), (15), and \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \dot\theta_b(s)
 &=\sum_x C_b(x)\dot\nu_x(s)+\sum_x\nu_x\dot C_b(x;s)\\
 &=E_0[\chi_b s]+\sum_xE_0[g^{\circ}_{b,x}s]
 =E_0\!\left[\left\{\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}\right\}s\right].
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{16}
\]
Thus the product-rule term is derived rather than absorbed into the causal target.

There are finitely many retained normals, so (14) implies \(\mathcal T_b(P_0)^{\perp}=\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}\). Combining this fact with (16) and \(\mathrm{def{:}influence\text{-}classes}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal I_b(P_0)=\chi_b+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}
 +\operatorname{span}\{R_{b,x}:x\in\mathcal X\}.
 \tag{17}
\]
The normalization gives \(E_0[R_{b,x}\mid G,X]=0\), while \(\chi_b\) is measurable with respect to \((G,X)\); hence \(E_0[R_b\chi_b]=0\). Put \(G_b^{\circ}=\sum_xg^{\circ}_{b,x}\), \(\Gamma_b=E_0[R_bR_b^{\prime}]\), and \(u_b=E_0[R_bG_b^{\circ}]\). If \(c\in\ker\Gamma_b\), then \(c^{\prime}R_b=0\) almost surely, so \(c^{\prime}u_b=0\); therefore \(u_b\in\operatorname{range}(\Gamma_b)\). Completing the square gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\chi_b+G_b^{\circ}+R_b^{\prime}a\|_2^2
 &=\|\chi_b+G_b^{\circ}-R_b^{\prime}\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b\|_2^2\\
 &\quad +(a+\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b)^{\prime}\Gamma_b
 (a+\Gamma_b^{\dagger}u_b).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{18}
\]
Minimization proves the displayed canonical-gradient formula. Finally, \(E_0[\chi_bg^{\circ}_{b,x}]=0\) by conditional centering, so the variance is \(E_0[\chi_b^2]\) plus the minimized centered-face variance.

Write \(E_0=E_{P_{0,O}}\), \(u=J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J\), and \(\mu_{C,t}(x)=(\mu_{2,t}(x),\ldots,\mu_{J+1,t}(x))^{\prime}\). The strict theorem-point conditions permit application of \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\); they do not alter either branch model.

We first relate the observed-law functionals to the causal ATT. Under conditional parallel trends and no anticipation,
\[
 \delta_1^0(x)=\Delta\mu_g(x),\qquad g=2,\ldots,J+1.
 \tag{1}
\]
It follows that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_F[Y_T(1)-Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]
 &=\mu_{1,T}(x)-\mu_{1,T-1}(x)-u^{\prime}D(x)\\
 &=C_{\mathrm{PT}}(x).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
Strict cell mass and overlap imply \(\pi_1=\sum_xp_X(x)p_1(x)>0\), so \(\nu_x=p_X(x)p_1(x)/\pi_1\) is well defined. Averaging (2) over \(X\mid G=1\) proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_O)\) on the PT branch.

Under the synthetic-mean restriction, the intercept and preperiod equations give \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\). The strict SC-rank condition makes \(B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\) invertible, so \(w(x)\) is uniquely identified by its displayed formula. The final-period equation gives
\[
 E_F[Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]=w(x)^{\prime}\mu_{C,T}(x),
 \tag{3}
\]
and hence the conditional causal effect equals \(C_{\mathrm{SC}}(x)\). Averaging proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_O)\) on the SC branch. At \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\), both equal the same conditional causal effect in every occupied stratum, so
\[
 C_{\mathrm{PT}}(x)=C_{\mathrm{SC}}(x),
 \qquad \chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0.
 \tag{4}
\]

Define the centered stratum faces
\[
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)=g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a,
 \qquad
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d.
 \tag{5}
\]
By \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\), adding \(\chi_0\) to sums of these faces exhausts the two influence classes. We prove that the classes meet. Suppress \(x\) and the common positive stratum factor. Adding a PT normal permits every donor vector \(v\) with \(\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}v=1\), giving the conditional-mean differential
\[
 L_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)=\dot\mu_{1,T}-\dot\mu_{1,T-1}
 -v^{\prime}(\dot\mu_{C,T}-\dot\mu_{C,T-1}).
 \tag{6}
\]
For SC, differentiating \(a=Bw\) and the full-rank least-squares formula gives
\[
 \dot w=(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B w).
 \tag{7}
\]
Consequently its affine face can be written
\[
 L_{\mathrm{SC}}(q)=\dot\mu_{1,T}-w^{\prime}\dot\mu_{C,T}
 +q^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B w),
 \qquad B^{\prime}q=-\mu_{C,T}.
 \tag{8}
\]
Indeed, one particular \(q\) represents the last term obtained by substituting (7), and adding \(\operatorname{range}(I_T-\Pi_x)=\ker(B^{\prime})\) generates every solution of the displayed affine constraint.

At the intersection, (1) gives \(\mu_{C,T}=\mu_{C,T-1}+\delta_x\mathbf 1_J\). Let \(e_0\) select the intercept row and \(e_-\) the period \(T-1\) row. Then \(B^{\prime}e_0=\mathbf 1_J\), \(B^{\prime}e_-=\mu_{C,T-1}\), and
\[
 q_*=-e_- -\delta_xe_0
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad B^{\prime}q_*=-\mu_{C,T}.
 \tag{9}
\]
The intercept rows are fixed, so \(e_0^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B w)=0\). Substituting (9) into (8) yields
\[
 L_{\mathrm{SC}}(q_*)
 =\dot\mu_{1,T}-\dot\mu_{1,T-1}
 -w^{\prime}(\dot\mu_{C,T}-\dot\mu_{C,T-1})
 =L_{\mathrm{PT}}(w).
 \tag{10}
\]
Restoring the stratum factor, (10) supplies equal centered representatives in every stratum. The product-rule contribution is already the common \(\chi_0\) in (4), proving that the full influence-class intersection is nonempty.

By the definitions of \(h_x\), \(\Omega_x\), and \(c(a,d)\),
\[
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)
 =c(a,d)^{\prime}h_x,
 \tag{11}
\]
and positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
 \Omega_x^{1/2}c(a,d)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 E_0[\{\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)\}^2\mid X=x]=0.
 \tag{12}
\]
The QP objective is \(E_0[\{\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)\}^2\mid X=x]\), and feasibility follows from (10). Projection onto the finite-dimensional closed affine feasible image gives a unique minimizing represented function; the Euclidean minimum-norm convention selects coefficients when displayed rows are redundant. The locally constant rank and strict positive-eigenvalue gap keep this coordinate representation stable.

Distinct strata have disjoint support. Conditional-residual normalization also gives
\[
 E_0[\chi_0\psi^{\circ}_{b,x}(a)]
 =E_0\!\left[\chi_0E_0\{\psi^{\circ}_{b,x}(a)\mid G,X\}\right]=0.
 \tag{13}
\]
Therefore the global projection separates into the common composition component and the stratum programs:
\[
 \phi_U=\chi_0+\sum_x\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^U)
 =\chi_0+\sum_x\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^U),
 \tag{14}
\]
and
\[
 V_U(P_0)=E_0[\chi_0^2]+\sum_xp_X(x)\min\mathrm{QP}_x.
 \tag{15}
\]

An estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) is regular along every quadratic-mean differentiable submodel in either branch, so its regular influence component belongs to both derivative classes. Applying \(\mathrm{lem{:}semiparametric\text{-}convolution\text{-}bound}\) to finite collections of such paths and then taking their closed span gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_0}(\text{regular limit})
 \ge \inf_{\phi\in\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)}E_0[\phi^2]
 =E_0[\phi_U^2].
 \tag{16}
\]
This is sharp as the canonical-gradient norm in the displayed local tangent experiment. Any estimator regular over the broader published union is regular on this subclass, so the inequality transfers by restriction. The cited Sun--Xie--Zhang result concerns one integrated estimator and one multiplier construction analyzed under the alternative branch hypotheses, with the branch-specific influence functions and variances recorded in \(\mathrm{lem{:}sun\text{-}xie\text{-}zhang\text{-}branchwise\text{-}laws}\). Nothing in (14)--(16) constructs attainment, a standard error, or multiplier inference.

Write \(E_0=E_{P_{0,O}}\) and \(\|f\|_0^2=E_0[f^2]\). The strict theorem-point conditions are exactly those required by the revised tangent-normal and union-envelope results. At the intersection, \(\chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0\). Define
\[
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)=g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a,
 \qquad
 \psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=g^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d.
 \tag{1}
\]
The tangent normal form, disjoint stratum support, and orthogonality of \(\chi_0\) to every conditional-residual piece show that the branch oracle projections separate by stratum:
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_0+\sum_x\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^{\mathrm{or}}),
 \qquad
 \phi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0+\sum_x\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^{\mathrm{or}}).
 \tag{2}
\]
Each branch variance is therefore \(E_0[\chi_0^2]\) plus its minimized centered-face variance. The common term cancels in the difference. By the definitions of \(h_x\), \(\Omega_x\), and \(c(a,d)\),
\[
 E_0[\{\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi^{\circ}_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)\}^2\mid X=x]
 =c(a,d)^{\prime}\Omega_xc(a,d).
 \tag{3}
\]
Since strict cell mass gives \(p_X(x)>0\), equations (2)--(3) imply
\[
 \|\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}-\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\|_0^2
 =\sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x^{\mathrm{or}})^{\prime}
 \Omega_xc(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x^{\mathrm{or}}).
 \tag{4}
\]
Every summand is nonnegative. Hence the simultaneous Gram discrepancy vanishes exactly when the two canonical gradients coincide in \(L^2(P_{0,O})\).

Let \(A=\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\), \(B=\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\), and \(C=A\cap B\). These are closed affine subsets of \(\mathcal H_{P_0}\), since their direction spaces are finite-dimensional normal spans, and \(C\ne\varnothing\) by \(\mathrm{thm{:}union\text{-}envelope}\). Let \(L_A\) be the direction space of \(A\). Minimality of \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\) gives \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\perp L_A\). For every \(c\in C\subseteq A\), the Pythagorean identity is therefore
\[
 \|c\|_0^2=\|\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\|_0^2+\|c-\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\|_0^2.
 \tag{5}
\]
Minimizing over \(C\) yields
\[
 V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in C
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\in B.
 \tag{6}
\]
Using (1)--(3), the squared distance from \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\) to \(B\) is
\[
 \min_{(d_x)}\sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x)^{\prime}
 \Omega_xc(a_x^{\mathrm{or}},d_x).
 \tag{7}
\]
The minimum is attained because it is a finite-dimensional positive-semidefinite least-squares problem; the Moore--Penrose convention handles redundant coordinates. Equations (6)--(7) prove the PT one-sided criterion. Interchanging the branches gives
\[
 V_U=V_{\mathrm{SC}}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \min_{(a_x)}\sum_xp_X(x)c(a_x,d_x^{\mathrm{or}})^{\prime}
 \Omega_xc(a_x,d_x^{\mathrm{or}})=0.
 \tag{8}
\]

If all three bounds coincide, (5) and its SC analogue force \(\phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\). Conversely, if the branch gradients coincide, their common value belongs to \(C\) and minimizes norm on both branch classes. Since \(C\) is contained in each branch class, it also minimizes norm on \(C\), so \(V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}=V_{\mathrm{SC}}\). Together with (4), this proves the simultaneous criterion. Every discrepancy is a function of \(p_X(x)\), \(\Omega_x\), and solutions of the finite covariance-weighted programs, so it is identified from \(P_{0,O}\). The argument uses no claim outside the displayed strict-interior constant-rank theorem point.

At the stated strict-interior constant-rank point, \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\) and \(\mathrm{thm{:}union\text{-}envelope}\) apply. If \(J=1\), then \(\mathbf 1_J\mathbf 1_J^{\prime}=1\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}restriction\text{-}maps}\) gives
\[
 A_{\mathrm{PT}}=I_1-1=0,
 \qquad r_{\mathrm{PT},x}=0.
 \tag{1}
\]
The tangent-normal form therefore gives
\[
 \mathcal T_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)=\mathcal H_{P_0},
 \qquad \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}\},
 \tag{2}
\]
where \(\phi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{PT}}+\sum_xg^{\circ}_{\mathrm{PT},x}\); in particular, the treated-composition term has not been dropped.

With one donor, the intercept row of the SC restriction forces \(w_2(x)=1\), while its preperiod equations give \(\mu_{1,t}(x)=\mu_{2,t}(x)\) for \(t<T\). Hence throughout the SC branch,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_O)
 &=\sum_x\nu_x\{\mu_{1,T}-\mu_{1,T-1}-\mu_{2,T}+\mu_{2,T-1}\}\\
 &=\sum_x\nu_x\{\mu_{1,T}-\mu_{2,T}\}
 =\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_O).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{3}
\]
Their derivatives agree on every SC tangent. Because the singleton PT influence function represents the PT derivative on all of \(\mathcal H_{P_0}\), it represents the common derivative on every SC tangent and therefore belongs to \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\). Thus
\[
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0),
 \qquad \phi_U=\phi_{\mathrm{PT}},
 \qquad V_U=V_{\mathrm{PT}}.
 \tag{4}
\]

For \(T=2\), write \(\Delta Y=Y_2-Y_1\) and \(m_g(x)=E_O[\Delta Y\mid G=g,X=x]\). The strict overlap conditions make every denominator positive. Direct quotient and conditional-mean differentiation yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \phi_{\mathrm{PT}}(O)
 &=\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=1\}}{\pi_1}\{\Delta Y-m_1(X)\}
 -\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=2\}}{\pi_1}\frac{p_1(X)}{p_2(X)}\{\Delta Y-m_2(X)\}\\
 &\quad+\frac{\mathbf 1\{G=1\}}{\pi_1}\{m_1(X)-m_2(X)-\theta\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{5}
\]
The first two terms are conditionally centered outcome-residual terms and the last is the treated-composition gradient. Their sum is mean zero, and its covariance with every score equals the derivative of the panel ATT functional. Under the group relabeling, (5) is the panel efficient influence function in SantAnnaZhao2020, Proposition 1(a), equation (2.11); equation (2.12) is its variance bound, exactly as recorded by \(\mathrm{lem{:}santanna\text{-}zhao\text{-}panel\text{-}did\text{-}gradient}\).

Fix \(x\) and put \(\Pi_x=B(x)\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}\). The strict SC-rank condition implies that \(B(x)\) has column rank \(J\), so \(\Pi_x\) is the orthogonal projector onto \(\operatorname{col}B(x)\) and \(I_T-\Pi_x\) has rank \(T-J\). The remaining strict margins ensure that this calculation occurs in the same two-sided constant-rank neighborhood used for the tangent construction.

At an SC law, \(a(x)=B(x)w(x)\). Differentiating the identity \(\Pi_xB(x)=B(x)\) gives
\[
 \dot\Pi_xB(x)w(x)=(I_T-\Pi_x)\dot B(x)w(x).
 \tag{1}
\]
Since \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=(I_T-\Pi_x)a(x)\), the product rule and (1) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \dot r_{\mathrm{SC},x}
 &=-\dot\Pi_xa(x)+(I_T-\Pi_x)\dot a(x)\\
 &=(I_T-\Pi_x)\{\dot a(x)-\dot B(x)w(x)\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{2}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}normal\text{-}gradients}\), \(R_{\mathrm{SC},x}\) is the conditionally centered Riesz vector for precisely (2). Conditional centering changes neither the deterministic range \(\operatorname{range}(I_T-\Pi_x)\) nor its dimension. Hence
\[
 \operatorname{range}E_0[R_{\mathrm{SC},x}R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}]
 \subseteq\operatorname{range}(I_T-\Pi_x),
\]
which proves the rank bound \(T-J\). If the residualized covariance form is positive definite on that range, its covariance kernel intersects the range only at zero, so its covariance rank equals \(\dim\operatorname{range}(I_T-\Pi_x)=T-J\).

Fix \(x\). When \(J=T\), \(B(x)\) is square. The strict SC-rank condition gives \(\lambda_{\min}\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}>\kappa_0>0\), so \(B(x)\) is invertible and
\[
 B(x)\{B(x)^{\prime}B(x)\}^{-1}B(x)^{\prime}=I_T.
 \tag{1}
\]
Thus \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0\) throughout the full-rank neighborhood. Its derivative and normalized Riesz vector are zero. The same conclusion follows from \(\mathrm{lem{:}sc\text{-}profiled\text{-}normal\text{-}rank}\), whose upper bound is \(T-J=0\).

All other strict theorem-point conditions permit use of \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\), which gives
\[
 \mathcal T_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)=\mathcal H_{P_0},
 \qquad
 \mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)

\[

 =\{\phi_{\mathrm{SC}}\}.
 \tag{3}
\]

There is one stratum and every group has probability \(1/3\). Hence \(p_X=1>\kappa_0\), while \(\epsilon_0<1/3<1-\epsilon_0\) because \(0<\epsilon_0<1/3\). No anticipation holds by construction. Every untreated final mean change is zero, so conditional parallel trends holds and
\[
 D=(0,0)^{\prime},\qquad \delta_1^0=0,
 \qquad q_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})=(0,0)^{\prime}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The augmented donor matrix and target vector are
\[
 B=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\-1&1\\-2&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad a=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad B^{\prime}B=\begin{pmatrix}6&-4\\-4&6\end{pmatrix}.
 \tag{2}
\]
The eigenvalues of \(B^{\prime}B\) are \(2\) and \(10\), both strictly larger than \(\kappa_0<1\). Solving \(Bw=a\) gives the unique weights \(w=(1/2,1/2)^{\prime}\), which also reproduce the period-three untreated mean. The strict fourth-moment hypothesis supplies strict moment slack. Hence \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_I\). In the coordinate order consisting of the two centered gradients, the two displayed PT-normal coordinates, and the three displayed SC-normal coordinates, direct multiplication using the innovation variances below gives the nonzero characteristic factor of \(\Omega\) as
\[
 p(\lambda)=\lambda^3-\frac{1563}{50}\lambda^2
 +\frac{415863}{1600}\lambda-\frac{10395}{16}.
 \tag{3a}
\]
The roots are real and positive because \(\Omega\) is a covariance matrix and (3a) is its nonzero factor. For \(u_j=\lambda_j-1\), their elementary symmetric functions are
\[
 \sum_ju_j=\frac{1413}{50}>0,\qquad
 \sum_{j<k}u_ju_k=\frac{320631}{1600}>0,\qquad
 \prod_ju_j=\frac{672053}{1600}>0.
 \tag{3b}
\]

Thus every \(u_j>0\), so every positive eigenvalue of \(\Omega\) exceeds \(1>\kappa_0\). Nonzero eigenvalues remain nonzero locally by continuity, giving locally constant rank. \[
 \chi_{\mathrm{PT}}=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}=\chi_0=0.
 \tag{3}
\]

Define \(z_{g,t}=3\mathbf 1\{G=g\}\varepsilon_{g,t}\). Quotient differentiation of a conditional cell mean shows that \(z_{g,t}\) is its mean-zero influence variable. \[
 (3,3,3),\qquad (3,3/2,3/2),\qquad (6,6,6).
 \tag{4}
\]
The PT face, parameterized by the donor-two weight \(v\), is
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)=(z_{1,3}-z_{1,2})
 -v(z_{2,3}-z_{2,2})-(1-v)(z_{3,3}-z_{3,2}).
 \tag{5}
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \|\psi_{\mathrm{PT}}(v)\|_0^2=6+3v^2+12(1-v)^2.
 \tag{6}
\]
The derivative is \(30v-24\), so the unique minimizer is \(v=4/5\), and
\[
 V_{\mathrm{PT}}(P^{\star})
 =6+3(4/5)^2+12(1/5)^2=\frac{42}{5}.
 \tag{7}
\]
For \(J=2\), the donor-change contrast has variance \(3+12=15>0\), so the PT normal Gram has rank one.

For SC, \(u=(0,-2,1)^{\prime}\) spans \(\ker(B^{\prime})\). Differentiating the full-rank normal equations gives
\[
 \dot w=(B^{\prime}B)^{-1}B^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B w).
 \tag{8}
\]
The unrestricted SC cell-mean coefficients, ordered by time within groups one, two, and three, are
\[
 (-2/5,-4/5,1),\qquad (1/5,2/5,-1/2),\qquad (1/5,2/5,-1/2).
 \tag{9}
\]
Adding \(\beta u^{\prime}(\dot a-\dot B w)\) changes only preperiod coefficients. Using (4), their variance contribution is
\[
 Q(\beta)=\frac{207}{8}\beta^2+\frac35\beta+\frac{99}{25}.
 \tag{10}
\]
This strictly convex quadratic is uniquely minimized at \(\beta^{\mathrm{or}}=-4/345\), with minimum \(91/23\). The final-period contribution is \(39/8\), and therefore
\[
 V_{\mathrm{SC}}(P^{\star})=\frac{39}{8}+\frac{91}{23}
 =\frac{1625}{184}.
 \tag{11}
\]

SC normals use only preperiod coordinates. Equality with the PT face therefore forces \(v=1/2\) from the final donor coefficients. Equality of the preperiod coefficients then forces \(\beta=-1/5\), producing the unique common representative with coefficients
\[

 \tag{12}
\]

\[

 \tag{13}
\]

\[

 \qquad V_U-V_{\mathrm{SC}}=\frac{169}{184}.
 \tag{14}

Choose the fixed constants so that \(P^{\star}\) satisfies every inequality defining the local class with strict slack and its finite Gram rank is locally constant. \[

 \tag{1}
\]
Give the treated group the same additive final treatment effect and call the law \(Q_\delta\). Every untreated final mean change remains zero, so PT holds. The donor matrix is unchanged, and the treated path is reproduced by the unique weights
\[

 \tag{2}
\]

There is one covariate stratum. On either branch \(C_b(X)=\theta_b\) is constant, hence
\[
 \chi_{\mathrm{PT}}(Q_\delta)=\chi_{\mathrm{SC}}(Q_\delta)=0.
 \tag{3}
\]

Fix an integer \(m\). Construct two triangular sequences that equal \(Q_\delta\) at coordinate \(m\) and \(P^{\star}\) at every other coordinate, labeling coordinate \(m\) by PT in the first and by SC in the second. Each is in \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\): after its exceptional coordinate it is identically \(P^{\star}\), so its QMD score and remainder are eventually zero, and every coordinate satisfies the fixed strict margins established above. \[
 \operatorname{Var}(z_{2,3})=\frac32,
 \qquad \operatorname{Var}(z_{3,3})=6.
 \tag{4}
\]
At \(P^{\star}\), the common score has final donor coefficients \((-1/2,-1/2)\). The PT extension freezes its center normal coefficient, while donor laws are unchanged, so its final donor coefficients remain \((-1/2,-1/2)\) at \(Q_\delta\). The SC normal uses only preperiod coordinates, whereas (2) makes the SC final donor coefficients \((-1/2-\delta,-1/2+\delta)\). Therefore, for
\[
 \Delta_\delta
 =\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{PT},P^{\star})
 -\phi_U^{\mathrm{loc}}(Q_\delta;\mathrm{SC},P^{\star}),
 \tag{5}
\]
the final-innovation component is \(\delta(z_{2,3}-z_{3,3})\). Every other component uses distinct group-period innovations and is orthogonal to this one. Consequently,
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 \ge\delta^2\left(\frac32+6\right)
 =\frac{15}{2}\delta^2>0.
 \tag{6}
\]
Both chart scores are mean zero, so \(E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta]=0\).

Suppose one estimator had both chart expansions uniformly over the frozen class. Couple the two sequences at sample size \(m\) through the same iid sample from \(Q_\delta\). The causal target is the same under the two labels because \(Q_\delta\in\mathcal M_I\). Subtracting the two asserted uniform expansions would give
\[
 S_m=m^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^m\Delta_\delta(O_i)=o_{Q_\delta}(1).
 \tag{7}
\]
By independent sampling and (6),
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2]=E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]
 \ge\frac{15}{2}\delta^2.
 \tag{8}
\]
Because \(\Delta_\delta\) is a bounded linear combination of finitely many Rademacher innovations,
\[
 E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^4]
 =m^{-1}E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^4]
 +3(1-m^{-1})E_{Q_\delta}[\Delta_\delta^2]^2
 \tag{9}
\]
is uniformly bounded. Hence \((S_m^2)\) is uniformly integrable. Convergence in probability in (7) would imply \(E_{Q_\delta}[S_m^2]\to0\), contradicting (8). Thus no estimator has both chart expansions uniformly over \(\mathfrak L_U(P^{\star})\). Since asymptotic linearity is a necessary conjunct of the requested one-step, variance-consistency, and multiplier-coverage result, the complete affirmative result is false. The argument proves no positive continuation theorem on any redesigned sequence class.
